question: Should OpenClaw sponsor the Claws core lifecycle and permit package-declared bootstrap files to become managed agent workspace instructions under this ownership model?
rationale: The patch can enforce filesystem and provenance mechanics, but automation cannot decide whether this persistent package lifecycle, trust boundary, and stacked public contract belong in OpenClaw core.

options.title: Pause pending RFC acceptance
options.body: Keep the protected stack open but do not land this slice until the RFC's lifecycle, package-content trust, and ownership contracts are explicitly accepted or narrowed.

options.title: Sponsor and complete proof
options.body: Approve the direction, preserve the current canonical schema design, and require exact-head real CLI proof before landing the stack in order.

options.title: Decline the core lifecycle
options.body: If this package model is not planned for core, close the implementation stack rather than continuing incremental repair work.

recommendation.title: Pause pending RFC acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep the protected stack open but do not land this slice until the RFC's lifecycle, package-content trust, and ownership contracts are explicitly accepted or narrowed.
